stem: The number of users of a new mobile payment app in Dhaka \(t\) months after its launch is modeled by \(N(t) = 2{,}000(1.1)^{t}\). According to the model, how many users will the app have 2 months after its launch?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(10\%\) of the starting value, 200, each month instead of growing by \(10\%\) of the current value.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying \(1.1\) by \(2\) instead of raising it to the power \(2\): \(2{,}000(2.2) = 4{,}400\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(N(1)\), the number of users after only 1 month.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'B': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
t = symbols('t')
N = Lambda(t, 2000*Rational(11, 10)**t)
assert N(2) == 2420
assert value(choices[answer]) == 2420
assert all(value(choices[k]) != 2420 for k in choices if k != answer)
